title: Output delta lab notes — quick evals and ad-hoc rubric
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Rough personal notebook for a handful of sample checks after we flipped the default quantization profile on dedicated staging nodes (q4_0 -> q4_1 mix).
- Not meant to be exhaustive; grabbing low-effort prompts that previously surfaced issues. Keep informal notes so we can decide whether to revert or tune kernels.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (0-3):
- Semantic fidelity: does the response preserve user intent and facts? (3=good, 0=broken)
- Hallucination: explicit incorrect facts or inventions (3=none, 0=lots)
- Conciseness / verbosity: 3=on-point, 1=rambling
- Token truncation / drop: 3=no drop, 0=noticeable cutoff mid-sentence
- Latency delta: rough median token latency change (ms) observed in traces
- Cost sig: ballpark cost/tokens delta relative to baseline

Test 1: policy-summary prompt (short doc)
Prompt:
"""Summarize the following privacy policy paragraph in 2-3 bullets suitable for product managers: 

"We collect device identifiers and usage telemetry to diagnose crashes and improve feature discovery. Data is aggregated and retained for up to 90 days. We do not share raw identifiers with third parties; we may share aggregated metrics."""

Baseline (q4_0, node: staged-01):
- "We collect device IDs and usage telemetry to diagnose crashes and improve feature discovery. Data is aggregated and kept for up to 90 days. Raw identifiers are not shared with third parties; only aggregated metrics may be shared."
Score baseline: semantic 3 / hallucination 3 / concision 3 / truncation 3 / latency baseline ~18ms/token

New (q4_1 mix, node: staged-01-quant):
- "We collect device identifiers and app telemetry to debug crashes and surface features. Aggregated metrics are retained up to three months. We never share user identifiers with external vendors, but we can provide summary stats."
Score new: semantic 2 (wording "never" is stronger than doc), hallucination 2 (adds "vendors"), concision 3, truncation 3, latency ~16ms/token, cost -6%
Notes: subtle strength shift ("never" vs "do not"). Could cause compliance flag if customers compare. Flagging as behavioral drift but not strictly incorrect. Ticket to check wording mapping in prompt->template rewrite (INFR-4271).

Test 2: multi-turn instruction (code generation minimal)
Prompt:
"""Given the snippet below, return a one-line explanation and the fix: 

function add(a,b){
 return a + b;
}

Call site: add('2', 3)"""

Baseline:
- Explanation: function adds two values; if called with a string and number JS coerces string, result '23'.
- Fix: coerce inputs to Number: return Number(a) + Number(b); or validate types.
Score baseline: semantic 3 / hallucination 3 / concision 3 / truncation 3 / latency ~22ms/token

New (q4_1):
- Explanation: adds two values; when mixing string and number it will produce 23 as a number.
- Fix: use parseInt on a, or use Number, or enforce types via TypeScript interface.
Score new: semantic 1 (mist states result type), hallucination 1 (asserts numeric 23), concision 2, truncation 3, latency ~19ms/token
Notes: This is an actual functional regression — incorrect claim about resulting type. Priority: high. Repro ticket created (JIRA INFR-4271). Add failing sample to unit/regression set.

Test 3: short Q/A (facts)
Prompt: "Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?"
Baseline: "Jane Austen." (score 3/3)
New: "Jane Austin." (typo) (score semantic 2/hallucination 2)
Notes: small character-level degradation; consider char-decoding kernel differences. Add to character-level QA set.

Observations / pattern hunting:
- Many regressions are subtle phrasing shifts (stronger adjectives like "never") and occasional small factual errors (char typos, numeric type mistakes) rather than wholesale nonsense.
- Latency generally improved slightly (~10-15%) under q4_1 mix; cost down ~5-8% in traces. Tradeoff: more brittle edge-case correctness.
- Failures frequently surface on short, highly-precise answers (code behavior, named entities). Longer freeform summaries less affected.

Immediate action items (for me):
- [ ] Add Test 2 (code-mix) as failing example to regression harness (file: /evals/regressions/output-deltas/code-mix-01.json) — note: create small canonicalized sample so CI catches it.
- [ ] Push a small config to try hybrid runtime: q4_1 for casual generation routes, q4_0 for code/fact routes (routing policy experiment). Draft config in PR referenced above.
- [ ] Run a small character-level QA sweep (500 examples) focusing on named entities -> collect edit distance distribution.
- [ ] Confirm whether decoding kernel change could introduce the "never" wording bias — ask @Leah Park to run beam vs sampling comparison on the same seed.

Open questions / random notes:
- Is the stronger negation language coming from compressed tokenization inducing different tokenization splits for common adverbs? (weird hypothesis)
- For the code example: did temperature or sampling shift? traces show same sampling params. Could be quantization-induced logit noise shifting argmax on short tokens.
- If we revert staging to q4_0, what will be the perf/cost delta on the nightly? approximate: +10% latency, +6% cost. Need ops signoff if we flip back.

Local quick checklist before sending to infra/ops:
- reproduce the code-mix failure on at least 3 different seeds/nodes (try tiny step: seed 42, 101, 202)
- capture token-level logits for the failing step (attach to PR)
- isolate if truncation or EOS token misfire is occurring (check KV cache lengths)

References / context links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (quant profiles changes)
- JIRA: INFR-4271 (regression: quantization output drift)
- Slack: #ml-infra thread ts=1700000000 (early discussion; Leah posted sample diffs)

Quick status log (mini-chron):
2025-11-03: quick pass, spotted code-mix error and naming typo.
2025-11-04: confirmed with Leah, added to regression set.
2025-11-08: tried hybrid routing experiment locally (toy) — promising.
2025-11-10: drafted this note, capturing immediate next steps.

Notes to self: keep this doc short-lived; transplant canonical failing samples into eval harness repo and then delete. If this grows, move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/ so others can iterate. 

-- Oliver
